newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Up a point, WPPSS revisits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Up a point, WPPSS revisits.

text.p: Municipals were lifted a solid point on Friday amid a frothy U.S. Treasury rally, while Goldman Sachs & Co took the opportunity to spring a second leg of Washington Public Power Supply System refunding bonds, traders said.
Goldman priced and repriced the issue of $246 million, ultimately lowering yields in several maturities. The top yield in 2012 was cut three basis points to 5.82 percent.
Friday's refunding marks WPPSS second visit to the market this week, and fulfills the utility's original plan for a $600 million refunding.
A total of $389 million insured refunding bonds were priced and repriced for a top yield of 5.91 percent in 2012.
Bonds from Tuesday's deal were freed to trade and bid at 5.82 percent "or better" near the close, one trader said.
Because the WPPSS deal was negotiated, the issuer was able to take advantage of quick market changes, said Richard Kolman, vice president and manager of underwriting and syndication at Goldman Sachs.
Turning to the municipal secondary, prices were quoted up one point in light to moderate trade.
A flurry of activity livened the Street in early trade as Treasuries rallied, one trader said, but that soon faded.

"There was some good bidding activity on the Street this morning, a few trades got done, but it was quick," one seasoned trader said. "It got to be that nobody would sell you anything, we had nothing to sell them, so the market was very thin to begin with."
Generic yield curve scales were marked up by about 10 basis points across the curve, one analyst said.

Long U.S. Treasuries sailed to more more than one point gains after the Labor Department said the overall and core components of its Consumer Price Index rose 0.1 percent in August. Economists in a Reuters poll expected both numbers to post gains of 0.2 percent.
Adding to the fervor, retail sales in August were also weak. The government said sales were up 0.2 percent for the month against forecasts for a 0.7 percent jump.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed up 1-15/32 to 97-14/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
Looking ahead, dealers noted supply is thin and well-picked giving the market a solid underpinning. Upcoming issues may therefore be bid aggressively despite a mounting calendar, one trader said.
In all, tax-exempt bond sales for the next week could total $2.23 billion, according to the Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Next week's competitive issues are topped by $200 million Massachusetts general obligation bonds and $100 million Ohio Capital Improvement bonds on Wednesday. Prior, players will vie for $101 million Tennessee School Authority GOs on Tuesday.

Negotiated issues feature $200 million San Diego County Regional Transportation Commission, Calif, revenue bonds and $100 million Honolulu, Hawaii, GOs, to be priced by Smith Barney Inc; $195 million Georgia Municipal Electric Authority revenue bonds, to be priced by J.P. Morgan Securities Inc; and $150 million Illinois Toll Highway Authority revenue bonds.
